study.title: Temporal-Spatial Feature Extraction of DSA Video and Its Application in AVM Diagnosis

imaging.modality_detail: Anteroposterior position 2D-DSA videos acquired on a Philips UNIQ FD20 biplane system; 6-s acquisition, 166-333 ms/frame
imaging.territory_detail: Cerebral angiography (ICA or VA injection) for brain arteriovenous malformation

annotation.annotator_expertise: Two specialists with >5 years in clinical cerebrovascular disease; a third senior doctor reviewed ambiguous cases

task.task_description: Faster-RCNN detects key vascular structures (ICA, circle of Willis, veins, venous vessels, venous sinuses) in each DSA frame; their order of appearance is encoded as five binary temporal features, fused with radiomics features from five equally spaced frames, and classified with sparse-representation feature selection plus SVM for AVM diagnosis and Spetzler-Martin high/low grading.
task.clinical_application: Automated diagnosis and grading of brain arteriovenous malformation on DSA

temporal_evidence.quote: the appearance order of important vascular structures was quantified as the temporal features

method.class_imbalance_handling: Spetzler-Martin grades merged into high (IV-V) vs low (I-III) classes due to small numbers and imbalance
method.explainability_method: Feature contribution from sparse representation coefficients
